actions.label: Have guards organize and implement distribution through guard structures
Deliver food rations into the camp on a continuing, long-term basis
Provide food rations to guards and their families, including as payment
Allow completion of FWB distribution documentation for donor accountability
Grant FWB staff escorted, coordinated camp access for food distribution
Distribute food equally to all refugee groups, including those labelled security threats
Stop diverting refugee and FWB food to guards
Permit an escorted FWB nutritional assessment
Consult refugees on their needs during distribution
Refrain from uncoordinated publicity and public reporting on the camp, acknowledging security challenges
Provide food assistance to affected host community households
Involve guard and militia structures in organizing and implementing distribution

goals.label: Burdensome external assessments and procedures imposed on the camp
Commander's authority and image of strength
FWB is neutral and independent of armed actors
FWB staff have access and freedom of movement in the camp
Food aid continues to flow into the camp long-term
Guards and militia control food distribution and camp operations
Guards and their families are fed and paid, keeping them loyal
Host town economy and goodwill, with local actors prioritized
Refugees actually receive adequate food intended for them
Refugees have a voice in the assistance they receive
Refugees remain contained in the camp and away from the capital
Safety of FWB staff and local assistants
Food aid is diverted to guards or militia, including as payment
Aid distribution is documented to meet donor accountability
Commander controls the narrative about the camp
Food is distributed fairly and impartially to all refugee groups
Refugees' nutritional needs are independently assessed
Relationship with and demands of the Senior Militia Leader

redLines.label: Allow FWB representatives and their local assistants to manage food disbursement directly
redLines.quote: If FWB hires local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

redLines.label: Have FWB staff and FWB-chosen local assistants directly manage food disbursement
redLines.quote: If FWB hires local independent laborers for the food distribution, you cannot trust those people not to stir unrest and even potentially support hidden terrorists by sharing items or information.

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
